model.name: Digital Signature / Proof
model.purpose: Describe a signature or cryptographic proof attached to a subject record: who or what signed, which verification method and suite were used, and what verification evidence exists — including the trust chain that connects the verification method to a trust anchor and the revocation-status evidence that qualifies it at a stated instant.
model.scope_statement: WM-XCT-034 is a mixin attachable to any model whose records can carry a signature or proof. It owns the description of the signature instance, the signer and verification-method reference, the signature suite and parameter references, and the verification evidence retained about that signature — the candidate and selected certification paths, the trust anchor and trust-store or trust-list snapshot in force, the revocation, suspension and supersession status evidence with its freshness fields, the instant against which the record is framed (current time, best-signature time, or a replayed historical instant), and the completeness or determinacy of that evidence. It carries references, captured evidence bytes, digests and validator-reported outcome codes. It does not operate certificate authorities, responders, trust-list schemes, DID resolvers or credential status publishers, does not execute cryptographic operations or the path-validation algorithm, does not decide or enforce trust policy, and does not own audit-trail semantics.
in_scope: Signature and proof instance records attached to a signed subject, as a mixin
Signer and verification-method references in every binding form: raw public key, X.509 end-entity certificate, verifiable credential and DID URL
Signature algorithm, suite and parameter references carried with the instance
Verification evidence retained about the signature, including validator-reported outcome codes carried verbatim
Candidate certification paths, their retrieval provenance, and the selected path
Basic-constraints, name-constraints, policy-constraints, key-usage and extended-key-usage inputs and recorded per-path outcomes
Trust anchor identity, anchor-carried path controls, and the pinned trust-store or trust-list snapshot version
Key and credential validity intervals, and observed compromise, revocation, suspension and supersession transitions
Captured CRL, delta CRL, OCSP and credential status-list evidence with thisUpdate/nextUpdate, reason codes, scope descriptors and digests
Status-evidence signer authorization basis, nonce binding, stapling and delivery channel
Validation instants: current time, best-signature time, and later historical replay, with proof-of-existence references
Evidence completeness and determinacy classification distinguishing evidence-incomplete from cryptographic failure
Long-term validation material references needed to replay a determination without contacting live services
out_of_scope: Certificate, credential and key issuance, and the act of revoking or suspending them
Operation of OCSP responders, CRL publication, delta-CRL scheduling and credential status-list publication
Trust-list scheme operation, supervision, qualification decisions and root-program admission
DID method operation, DID document lifecycle, and directory or resolver operation
Runtime cryptographic execution, key generation, key storage, key destruction and HSM governance
Policy decision, policy enforcement and access-authorization outcomes derived from a verification result
Audit-trail and event-log record semantics, retention and tamper evidence
Time-stamp token issuance and time-stamping authority governance
Identity proofing, subject vetting and registration authority procedures
The domain semantics, meaning or business effect of whatever content was signed

boundary_notes.neighbor: Certificate authority and trust service operations model
boundary_notes.distinction: That model owns issuance, the decision to revoke or suspend, the revocation date it publishes, and responder operation. This mixin carries only references to issuer and responder records, captured evidence bytes and the observed transition with its observation time; it never asserts a revocation itself.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Trust list and trust anchor store governance model
boundary_notes.distinction: That model operates the list, determines service status and publishes sequence-numbered issues. This mixin pins the snapshot by scheme operator, sequence number, issue date-time and digest, and records the status it observed at the validation instant.

boundary_notes.neighbor: DID method registry and DID resolution infrastructure
boundary_notes.distinction: Resolution, DID document versioning and deactivation belong to the DID method and its resolver. This mixin carries the DID URL, the resolution options supplied, the returned resolution metadata and the version reference in effect.

Whether missing or stale status evidence produces acceptance or rejection is a policy decision. This mixin records the declared stance as a reference to its declaring authority and never selects a universal hard-fail, soft-fail or treat-as-unknown rule.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Cryptographic execution and algorithm registry model
boundary_notes.distinction: Signature verification arithmetic, algorithm implementation and deprecation schedules sit outside. This mixin references the suite identifier and carries the outcome reported by whatever executed the operation.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Audit trail and event log model
boundary_notes.distinction: Referencing an audit record does not grant ownership of audit semantics. A replay package here is an evidence container, not an audit record; audit entries are located by reference only.
Token issuance, timestamping authority trust and archival preservation belong elsewhere. This mixin references a proof of existence to frame best-signature time and historical replay.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Signed subject model (the record carrying the signature)
boundary_notes.distinction: The subject model owns the content, its meaning and its own lifecycle. This mixin attaches signature and proof context without altering or duplicating subject semantics.

sources.title: RFC 5280: Internet X.509 Public Key Infrastructure Certificate and Certificate Revocation List (CRL) Profile
sources.relevance: Normative source for certification path validation inputs and algorithm (clause 6), basic constraints, name constraints, policy constraints, key usage and extended key usage, and the CRL profile including thisUpdate, nextUpdate, revocationDate, reason codes, certificateHold, removeFromCRL, delta CRLs and issuing distribution point (clause 5).

sources.title: RFC 6960: X.509 Internet Public Key Infrastructure Online Certificate Status Protocol - OCSP
sources.relevance: Normative source for CertID scope, good/revoked/unknown statuses (2.2), thisUpdate/nextUpdate/producedAt semantics (2.4), pre-produced responses (2.5), delegated responder authorization and id-kp-OCSPSigning and ocsp-nocheck (2.6, 4.2.2.2), response acceptance conditions (3.2), the nonce extension (4.4.1) and archive cutoff (4.4.4).

sources.title: RFC 4158: Internet X.509 Public Key Infrastructure: Certification Path Building
sources.relevance: Establishes the separation of path building from path validation, the existence of multiple candidate paths in mesh and bridge architectures, retrieval sources (AIA, SIA, LDAP, caches), sorting and elimination heuristics, loop control by repeated subject-name and key pairs, and separate path building for revocation signer certificates.

sources.title: RFC 5914: Trust Anchor Format
sources.relevance: Defines TrustAnchorInfo (pubKey, keyId, taTitle, certPath, exts) and CertPathControls (taName, certificate, policySet, policyFlags, nameConstr, pathLenConstraint), and the notion of a trust anchor list or store, grounding trust-anchor identity and anchor-carried path controls.

sources.title: RFC 9608: No Revocation Available for X.509 Public Key Certificates
sources.relevance: Defines the noRevAvail extension and modifies RFC 5280 path validation so revocation checking is skipped when noRevAvail or ocsp-nocheck is present; the counterexample proving that absent status evidence is not always incomplete evidence.

sources.title: RFC 9919: The Lightweight Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP) Profile for High-Volume Environments
sources.relevance: Normative source for nonce omission and the requirement to ignore a nonce when none was sent, mandatory nextUpdate for caching, GET and HTTP cache behaviour, pre-produced response distribution, and configurable clock-skew tolerance around nextUpdate.

sources.title: RFC 7633: X.509v3 Transport Layer Security (TLS) Feature Extension
sources.relevance: Shows that hard-fail on missing stapled status evidence is only well-founded when the certificate itself declares the required feature, and that a relying party can otherwise draw no conclusion from absent in-band status information.

sources.title: Decentralized Identifiers (DIDs) v1.1
sources.relevance: Defines verification method properties (id, type, controller, publicKeyJwk, publicKeyMultibase) in clause 5.2 and the verification relationships authentication, assertionMethod, keyAgreement, capabilityInvocation and capabilityDelegation in clause 5.3, grounding non-X.509 verification-method binding and declared purpose.

sources.title: DID Resolution v1.0
sources.relevance: Defines resolution options (accept, versionId, versionTime), resolution metadata (contentType, error), DID document metadata (created, updated, deactivated, versionId, nextVersionId, canonicalId, equivalentId) and error codes, grounding captured resolution inputs and version references without owning resolver operation.

sources.title: Bitstring Status List v1.0
sources.relevance: Defines credentialStatus, BitstringStatusListEntry (statusListIndex, statusListCredential, statusSize, statusMessage) and statusPurpose values revocation, suspension, message and refresh, plus validFrom/validUntil, ttl and herd-privacy caching guidance for credential status evidence.

sources.title: DSS Documentation - Digital Signature Service (eSignature building block)
sources.organization: European Commission, Directorate-General for Digital Services
sources.relevance: First-party reference documentation of the European Commission implementation of ETSI EN 319 102-1, enumerating the indications TOTAL_PASSED, TOTAL_FAILED and INDETERMINATE and sub-indications including REVOKED_NO_POE, OUT_OF_BOUNDS_NO_POE, TRY_LATER, NO_CERTIFICATE_CHAIN_FOUND and CRYPTO_CONSTRAINTS_FAILURE_NO_POE, and describing proof of existence, best-signature time, revocation freshness and trusted-list handling per ETSI TS 119 612 and TS 119 615.

sources.title: EU List of Trusted Lists (LOTL)
sources.relevance: Live primary artifact demonstrating trust-list snapshot fields actually in use: TSLVersionIdentifier, TSLSequenceNumber, TSLType, SchemeOperatorName, SchemeTerritory, StatusDeterminationApproach, HistoricalInformationPeriod, ServiceDigitalIdentity with X509Certificate, TSLLocation and the ETSI TSL MIME type.

sources.title: Baseline Requirements for the Issuance and Management of Publicly-Trusted TLS Server Certificates
sources.relevance: Root-program-facing operational requirements showing that a CA must make revocation information available for subordinate and subscriber certificates (clause 2.1), and evidence that publicly-trusted TLS practice constitutes one operational stance among several rather than a universal rule.

bundles.name: Trust-path and verification-method context
bundles.description: Everything needed to state which verification method a signature depends on, how that method is reached from a trust anchor, and under which anchor-level and path-level constraints that reachability was recorded.
bundles.rationale: Path building and path validation are distinct concerns (SRC-003), and both are meaningless without a pinned anchor and anchor-carried controls (SRC-004). Non-X.509 verification methods reach the same question through a different binding (SRC-008), so the binding form must be modelled before the chain. Grouping these three concerns keeps the reachability question separate from the status question, which changes on a different clock.

layers.name: Verification-method reference and declared purpose
layers.description: How the signature record points at the material used to verify it, in each supported binding form, and what that material declares about the purposes it may be used for.

findings.name: Verification-method reference and resolution inputs
findings.description: The reference that identifies the verification key material for a signature — a raw public key, an X.509 end-entity certificate, a verifiable credential, or a DID URL — together with the resolution inputs supplied and the resolution metadata and version reference returned. The external record itself is owned and operated by its issuer, controller or DID method; this finding captures the pointer and what was observed when it was retrieved.

questions.text: Which identifier resolves the verification method used for this signature, and in which identifier space is that identifier authoritative?
answer_data: Verification-method identifier, DID URL, or issuer name plus certificate serial number
Identifier space or namespace authority
Controller or issuer identifier

questions.text: Which binding form carries the verification key: bare public key, X.509 certificate, verifiable credential, or DID document entry?
answer_data: Binding form code
Key material encoding such as SubjectPublicKeyInfo, publicKeyJwk or publicKeyMultibase
Media type of the retrieved representation

questions.text: What resolution inputs were supplied and what resolution metadata was returned when the verification method was retrieved?
answer_data: Resolution options supplied, such as accept, versionId or versionTime
Resolution metadata returned, including contentType and any error code
Retrieval endpoint and retrieval observation time

questions.text: Which version of the verification-method record was in effect, and how would a later version be distinguished from the one actually used?
answer_data: Document versionId and nextVersionId, or certificate validity interval
Created and updated timestamps of the external record
Deactivated or superseded flag as reported by the source

data_elements.name: Verification method reference
data_elements.description: Authoritative pointer to the verification key material relied on by this signature.

data_elements.name: Binding form code
data_elements.description: Which form of verification-method binding applies: raw key, X.509 certificate, credential or DID document entry.

data_elements.name: Key material encoding
data_elements.description: Encoding of the public key as retrieved, for example SubjectPublicKeyInfo, publicKeyJwk or publicKeyMultibase.

data_elements.name: Resolution metadata capture
data_elements.description: Options supplied to and metadata returned by the external resolution step, captured verbatim.

data_elements.name: Verification method version reference
data_elements.description: Version identifier or validity interval that pins which state of the external record was used.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The verification-method record is created, versioned and published by an external certificate authority, credential issuer or DID method, and copying it here would duplicate a record whose lifecycle this model does not own. What this finding contributes is purely reference and observation data: the pointer, the binding form, the options supplied to resolution, the metadata returned and the version pinned. Where certificate bytes are actually retained, they are retained as part of the certification path certificate set in the path layer, not duplicated here.

findings.name: Declared purpose and usage constraints of the verification method
findings.description: What the verification method itself declares about the operations it may be used for, and what relying-party behaviour it demands — key usage bits, extended key usage purposes, DID verification relationships, and certificate-declared mandatory relying-party features. Whether a mismatch is tolerated is a policy decision made elsewhere; this finding records the declaration and the observed mismatch.

questions.text: For which purposes was this verification method authorized, and where is each authorization declared?
answer_data: keyUsage bits asserted
extendedKeyUsage purpose identifiers
DID verification relationships such as authentication or assertionMethod

questions.text: What is recorded when the declared purpose does not cover the operation this signature was actually used for?
answer_data: Purpose mismatch flag
Declared purpose set
Purpose the signature was relied on for

questions.text: Does the verification method assert a mandatory relying-party feature such as stapled status evidence?
answer_data: Declared mandatory feature identifiers
Criticality of the declaring extension
Whether the feature was satisfied in the observed exchange

questions.text: Which controller or issuer asserts control over this verification method, and how is that assertion evidenced?
answer_data: Controller or issuer identifier
Control assertion location, such as the controller property or issuer distinguished name
Reference to the evidence supporting the control assertion

data_elements.name: Key usage set
data_elements.description: Key usage bits asserted by the verification method for this signature.

data_elements.name: Extended key usage set
data_elements.description: Extended key usage purpose identifiers asserted by the verification method.

data_elements.name: Verification relationship
data_elements.description: Declared relationship such as authentication, assertionMethod, keyAgreement, capabilityInvocation or capabilityDelegation.

data_elements.name: Mandatory relying-party feature
data_elements.description: Feature the certificate demands of a relying party, such as required stapled status evidence.

data_elements.name: Controller reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the controller or issuer asserting control over the verification method.

findings.inline_only_rationale: These are declarations already carried inside an external certificate, credential or DID document; extracting them into a separate artifact would create a second, divergable copy of bytes this model does not own. They are recorded as normalized inline fields alongside a pointer to the declaring extension or property, so a reader can re-derive them from the captured path certificate set when needed.

layers.name: Certification path, constraints and trust-anchor context
layers.description: The candidate paths considered, the path actually selected and by which builder, the constraint inputs and recorded per-path outcomes, and the trust anchor and trust-store snapshot that terminated the path.

findings.name: Candidate certification paths, retrieval provenance and selection
findings.description: The set of candidate paths assembled toward a trust anchor, where each intermediate certificate came from, which candidate was selected, and by which external path builder on what recorded ordering criteria. Path building is a search that may yield several defensible answers in mesh and bridge architectures, so the alternatives and the selection basis are context in their own right.

questions.text: Which candidate certification paths were assembled for this signature, and how is each candidate identified?
answer_data: Candidate path identifier
Ordered certificate references forming the candidate
Candidate path length

questions.text: From which store, extension or protocol message was each intermediate certificate obtained?
answer_data: Retrieval source such as authority information access, subject information access, directory, local cache or embedded certificate bag
Retrieval endpoint or container reference
Retrieval observation time

questions.text: Which candidate path was selected, by which builder, and on what recorded ordering or elimination criteria?
answer_data: Selected candidate identifier
Path builder identity and version
Recorded sorting and elimination criteria applied

questions.text: How were repeated subject-name and public-key pairs detected and excluded from candidate paths?
answer_data: Loop-control rule applied
Excluded candidate references
Basis on which repetition was detected

data_elements.name: Candidate path identifier
data_elements.description: Local identifier for one assembled candidate certification path.

data_elements.name: Path certificate reference
data_elements.description: Ordered reference to a certificate in a candidate path, by issuer name and serial number.

data_elements.name: Path certificate retrieval source
data_elements.description: Where a path certificate was obtained from, including the extension or store used.

data_elements.name: Selected path reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the candidate path selected for the recorded determination.

data_elements.name: Path builder identity
data_elements.description: Identity and version of the external component that assembled and ordered the candidates.

artifacts.name: Certification path certificate set
artifacts.description: The captured, byte-preserving set of certificates forming the candidate and selected paths, retained so the path can be re-presented to a validator without re-contacting directories or authority information access endpoints.
media_or_form: Certificate bag embedded in the signed data object
JSON Web Key set or credential collection for non-X.509 bindings
artifacts.identity_strategy: Each contained certificate is identified by the authoritative master-system identifier assigned by its issuing certification authority — issuer name plus certificate serial number. The captured set as a whole is identified by a digest over the concatenated DER bytes in path order, with a Dimension-assigned ULID used only as a local handle. No issue date or validity bound is used as an identifier.

findings.name: Path validation inputs and recorded constraint outcomes
findings.description: The initial inputs supplied to path validation and the per-certificate and per-path constraint outcomes recorded afterwards: basic constraints and path length, name constraints against tested name forms, certificate policies and policy mappings, and unrecognized critical extensions. The algorithm is executed by an external validator; this finding records what was fed in and what came back so the determination is reproducible.

questions.text: Which initial path-validation inputs were supplied for this determination?
answer_data: Initial policy set
Initial explicit-policy, policy-mapping-inhibit and any-policy-inhibit flags
Initial permitted subtrees and initial excluded subtrees

questions.text: What basic-constraints and path-length outcome was recorded for each certification authority certificate in the selected path?
answer_data: Certification authority boolean per certificate
Path length constraint value per certificate
Recorded outcome per certificate position

questions.text: Which name constraints applied, and which subject and alternative name forms were tested against them?
answer_data: Permitted subtrees in force at each position
Excluded subtrees in force at each position
Name forms tested and the per-name result

questions.text: Which certificate policies and policy mappings survived to the end of the selected path?
answer_data: Authorities-constrained or user-constrained policy set at path end
Policy mapping records applied along the path
Explicit-policy state at path end

questions.text: How is an unrecognized critical extension encountered in the path recorded?
answer_data: Extension object identifier
Criticality flag as encoded
Recorded handling outcome reported by the validator

data_elements.name: Initial policy set
data_elements.description: Set of certificate policy identifiers acceptable to the relying party for this determination.

data_elements.name: Path control flags
data_elements.description: Initial inhibit and require flags supplied for policy processing.

data_elements.name: Name constraint outcome
data_elements.description: Per-name-form result of testing subject and alternative names against permitted and excluded subtrees.

data_elements.name: Path length outcome
data_elements.description: Remaining permitted intermediate count recorded at a certificate position in the selected path.

data_elements.name: Unrecognized critical extension
data_elements.description: Object identifier of a critical extension the validator did not recognize, with its recorded handling.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Constraint inputs and outcomes are structured scalar and set-valued fields, not documents. They must be stored inline so that a later replay can re-supply exactly the same inputs to a validator and compare against exactly the same recorded outcomes; encapsulating them in an artifact would obscure field-level comparison. The extension bytes they derive from are already retained inside the certification path certificate set artifact, so no second copy is warranted.

findings.name: Trust anchor identity, anchor-carried controls and trust-store snapshot
findings.description: The trust anchor that terminated the selected path, the path controls the anchor itself imposes below it, the trust store or trust list snapshot that made the anchor trusted at the recorded instant, and the service status the governing list reported for it. Operation of the store or list — admission, supervision, status determination — belongs to its scheme operator.

questions.text: Which trust anchor terminated the selected path, and by which name and key identifier is it recorded?
answer_data: Trust anchor name
Public key identifier of the anchor
Reference to the anchor certificate or trust anchor information object if one exists

questions.text: Which path controls does the trust anchor itself impose on certification paths beneath it?
answer_data: Anchor policy set
Anchor policy flags for inhibit policy mapping, require explicit policy and inhibit any policy
Anchor name constraints and path length constraint

questions.text: Which trust store or trust list snapshot was in force, and how is that snapshot pinned so it can be reproduced?
answer_data: Trust store or trust list identifier and location
Sequence number, version identifier and issue date-time of the snapshot
Digest over the retrieved snapshot bytes

questions.text: What status did the governing trust list report for the anchor's trust service at the recorded instant?
answer_data: Service status identifier as published
Current status starting date and time
Service type identifier and scheme territory

data_elements.name: Trust anchor name
data_elements.description: Distinguished name or equivalent name of the trust anchor terminating the selected path.

data_elements.name: Trust anchor key identifier
data_elements.description: Public key identifier of the trust anchor, used to distinguish re-keyed anchors sharing a name.

data_elements.name: Anchor path controls
data_elements.description: Policy set, policy flags, name constraints and path length constraint carried by the anchor itself.

data_elements.name: Trust store snapshot reference
data_elements.description: Pinned reference to the trust store or trust list issue in force, by location, sequence number and digest.

data_elements.name: Observed trust service status
data_elements.description: Status the governing trust list published for the anchor's service, with its status starting date and time.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Trust anchor sets and trust lists are published, sequence-numbered artifacts operated by scheme operators and root programmes that this model explicitly does not own; retaining a local copy as an owned artifact would imply custody of a list whose issuance and status determination happen elsewhere. The defensible contribution is a pin: location, sequence number, issue date-time, digest and the status observed, all of which are reference and scalar values. A consumer that needs the bytes fetches the pinned issue from its operator and verifies the recorded digest.

bundles.name: Revocation-status evidence and temporal determinacy
bundles.description: Everything needed to state what the authoritative status source said about the verification method, how trustworthy and fresh that statement is, against which instant the whole record is framed, and whether the evidence is complete enough to be determinate at all.
bundles.rationale: Status evidence has its own issuance clock, its own signer and its own authorization chain, all independent of the certification path (SRC-002, SRC-006). Correctness at the current instant, at best-signature time and on later historical replay are three different questions over the same evidence (SRC-011), and absent evidence can be normatively correct rather than a gap (SRC-005). Separating this bundle from the path bundle prevents collapsing 'evidence missing' into 'signature invalid'.

layers.name: Status mechanism, evidence record and its authorization
layers.description: Which status mechanism governs the verification method, what the captured evidence says and about what scope, who was authorized to sign it, and how it was bound to this request and delivered.

findings.name: Status mechanism and captured status determination
findings.description: The mechanism that governs status for this verification method, the status value reported with its reason and effective date, whether that status is reversible, and the scope the evidence claims to cover. Mechanism-specific vocabularies are kept distinct rather than normalized, because suspension, hold and supersession do not map cleanly across certificate revocation lists, online status responses and credential status lists.

questions.text: Which status mechanism governs this verification method, and what does the certificate or credential itself declare about it?
answer_data: Mechanism code covering certificate revocation list, delta list, online status protocol, credential status list, or declared-unavailable
Declared distribution point and responder location identifiers
Presence of a no-revocation-available or responder-no-check declaration

questions.text: What status value was reported for the subject, with which reason code and effective date?
answer_data: Status value in the mechanism's own vocabulary, including the unknown case
Reason code as published by the source
Effective date of the status, distinct from when the evidence was issued

questions.text: Is the reported status reversible, and how are suspension and supersession distinguished from permanent revocation?
answer_data: Reversibility indicator and status purpose such as revocation, suspension, message or refresh
Hold and release-from-hold indications where the mechanism supports them
Superseded indication with a reference to the successor verification method

questions.text: What scope does this status evidence claim to cover, and does the subject demonstrably fall inside it?
answer_data: Scope descriptor such as issuing distribution point, indirect-issuer indication or delta-list base reference
Subject match fields such as issuer name hash, issuer key hash and serial number, or status list index and list credential reference
In-scope determination with its basis

data_elements.name: Status mechanism code
data_elements.description: Which status mechanism produced or is declared to govern this determination.

data_elements.name: Reported status value
data_elements.description: Status value in the reporting mechanism's own vocabulary, retained without cross-mechanism normalization.

data_elements.name: Status reason code
data_elements.description: Reason published with the status, such as key compromise, superseded, cessation of operation or hold.

data_elements.name: Status effective time
data_elements.description: Time from which the reported status applies, as published by the authoritative source.

data_elements.name: Status evidence scope descriptor
data_elements.description: Fields describing what population the evidence covers and how the subject was matched into it.

artifacts.name: Captured revocation status evidence object
artifacts.description: The byte-preserving capture of the signed status statement relied on — a certificate revocation list, a delta list, a signed online status response, or a status list credential — retained so the determination can be re-verified without re-contacting the issuing source.
media_or_form: DER-encoded certificate list, full or delta
DER-encoded signed online certificate status response
Revocation-values container embedded in a signed data object
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified first by the authoritative master-system identifier assigned by the issuing source: certificate revocation list issuer plus certificate revocation list number, or responder key identifier plus the certificate identifier and production time for an online response. Where the mechanism assigns no series number, the governed global identifier is used — the status list credential reference plus index. A Dimension-assigned ULID plus a digest over the exact retrieved bytes is the last resort. Issue dates, this-update and next-update values are never used as identifiers.

findings.name: Status-evidence authorization, replay binding and delivery
findings.description: Who signed the captured status evidence, on what basis that signer was authorized to speak for the subject, how the recursion into the signer's own status was stopped, what binds the evidence to this request rather than to a replayed earlier one, and through which channel and cache it arrived. The signer's certificate and the responder service are operated externally; this finding records the authorization basis reported and the binding fields observed.

questions.text: Who signed the captured status evidence, and on what basis was that signer authorized to speak for this subject?
answer_data: Status signer identifier and key identifier
Delegation basis, such as signing by the same key as the issuing authority, a delegated signing purpose identifier, or a trust list entry
Reference to the separately built certification path for the status signer

questions.text: How was the status signer's own revocation position handled without recursing without bound?
answer_data: Presence of a responder-no-check declaration or a no-revocation-available declaration
Reference to status evidence for the signer, or an explicit recorded omission
Recursion-stop rule that was applied and who declared it

questions.text: What binds this status evidence to this particular request rather than to an earlier response replayed at us?
answer_data: Nonce present, omitted or ignored, with the match result where present
Production time and any request correlation identifier
Whether the profile in use permits nonce omission, and which profile version

questions.text: Through which channel and cache did the evidence arrive: stapled in protocol, fetched directly, embedded in the signed data object, or served from cache?
answer_data: Delivery channel code
Cache origin, cache directives observed and cache age at use
Request method and endpoint where a fetch occurred

data_elements.name: Status signer reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the entity whose key signed the captured status evidence.

data_elements.name: Status signer delegation basis
data_elements.description: Recorded basis on which the status signer was accepted as authorized for the subject.

data_elements.name: Nonce binding state
data_elements.description: Whether a nonce was sent, returned, matched, omitted or deliberately ignored under the profile in use.

data_elements.name: Evidence delivery channel
data_elements.description: How the status evidence reached the relying party, including whether it was stapled or served from cache.

data_elements.name: Evidence digest
data_elements.description: Digest and digest algorithm over the exact retrieved status evidence bytes.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The status signer's certificate, its own certification path and the responder service are external records operated by a certification authority or responder operator, and the transport that delivered the evidence is a protocol exchange this model does not own. What remains is a set of scalar and reference fields — signer pointer, delegation basis, nonce state, channel, cache age, digest — which must sit inline next to the evidence object they qualify. The evidence bytes themselves are already held by the captured status evidence object artifact in this same layer, so a second artifact would duplicate custody.

layers.name: Validation instants and evidence determinacy
layers.description: The instant a trust-chain record is framed against, the proof of existence that supports a past instant, the separation of event time from observation time, and whether the assembled evidence is complete enough to be determinate.

findings.name: Validation instant, proof of existence and observation time
findings.description: Which instant this trust-chain record is framed against — the current time, the best-signature time established by a proof of existence, or a replayed historical instant — together with the proof that supports a past instant, the separation of when facts occurred from when they were observed, and the clock-skew tolerance assumed when comparing an instant to an evidence window. A signature made before revocation and proven to predate it is a different case from one made after, and the model must be able to state which case it is describing.

questions.text: Against which instant is this trust-chain record framed: current time, best-signature time, or a replayed historical instant?
answer_data: Instant kind code
Instant value expressed with seconds and an explicit offset
Reference to the rule or request that selected this instant

questions.text: What proof of existence establishes that the signature and its supporting evidence existed before the claimed instant?
answer_data: Reference to the proof of existence, such as a time-stamp token, ledger entry or archival record
Issuer identifier of the proof
Description of what the proof demonstrably covers

answer_data: Event time as published by the authoritative source
Observation or ingestion time recorded by this model
Identifier of the system that performed the observation

answer_data: Inventory of evidence required for replay
Retention horizon reference and any archive-cutoff value reported by the source
Replay-completeness flag for the declared instant

answer_data: Tolerance value and unit
Time source reference used by the recording system
Comparison rule applied to the this-update and next-update bounds

data_elements.name: Validation instant kind
data_elements.description: Whether the record is framed at current time, at best-signature time, or at a replayed historical instant.

data_elements.name: Validation instant value
data_elements.description: The instant itself, recorded with seconds and an explicit offset.

data_elements.name: Proof of existence reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the external proof that fixes the signature or evidence before the claimed instant.

data_elements.name: Observation time
data_elements.description: Time at which this model captured the fact, held separately from the fact's own event time.

data_elements.name: Clock skew tolerance
data_elements.description: Tolerance applied when comparing an instant against evidence validity bounds.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Instants, tolerances and observation times are scalar values, and the proof of existence they lean on is a token issued and governed by a separate time-stamping or preservation authority that this model references rather than owns. Storing these inline keeps the temporal frame directly comparable with the this-update and next-update bounds recorded on the evidence object, which is exactly the comparison a replay must repeat. The assembled replay container that packages them is declared separately under the determinacy finding.

findings.name: Evidence completeness and determinacy classification
findings.description: Whether the assembled trust-chain and status record is complete enough at the declared instant to be determinate, or whether it is evidence-incomplete — missing, stale, out of scope, or unreachable — as distinct from a cryptographic failure. Also carries, verbatim and attributed, any validation indication issued by an external validator, and the failure-handling stance declared by the consuming environment. The model classifies the completeness of its own record; it does not decide trust and does not enforce an outcome.

questions.text: Which required trust-chain and status elements are present, stale or missing for the declared instant?
answer_data: Presence flag per required element
Staleness measured against the evidence next-update bound
Inventory of missing or unreachable elements with the reason recorded

questions.text: Is this record determinate, or is it evidence-incomplete rather than cryptographically failed?
answer_data: Determinacy class covering determinate, evidence-incomplete and not-assessed
Distinguishing reason, including whether absent status was declared unavailable by the issuer
Cryptographic verification outcome carried as a separate field, never merged into the determinacy class

answer_data: Indication value carried verbatim in the issuing vocabulary
Sub-indication value carried verbatim
Issuing validator identity, version and the validation policy reference it applied

Identifier of the authority or policy record that declared the stance
Scope over which the declared stance applies

answer_data: Whether the status was obtained by direct query, stapling, cached list or embedded material
Query-linkability indicator for the channel used
Applied minimization or aggregation measure recorded with the capture

data_elements.name: Determinacy class
