data_elements.description: Top-level indication issued by an external validator, carried verbatim with its issuing vocabulary.

data_elements.name: Carried validation sub-indication
data_elements.description: Sub-indication issued by an external validator, carried verbatim with its issuing vocabulary.

data_elements.name: Declared failure-handling stance reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the externally declared stance for missing or stale status evidence, with its declaring authority.

artifacts.name: Trust-chain evidence replay package
artifacts.description: A self-contained container assembling the selected path, the trust-anchor and trust-store pin, every captured status evidence object, the declared instant and proof-of-existence references, and the determinacy record, so that an external validator can re-evaluate the same determination later without contacting live services.
media_or_form: Archival container bundling path certificates, status evidence and instant records
Long-term validation material container embedded in a signed data object
Detached evidence manifest listing member digests and their pinned references
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the authoritative master-system identifier of the signed subject the mixin is attached to, plus the package owner and a monotonic package sequence number assigned by the adopting Dimension. Where no master-system identifier exists for the subject, a governed global identifier for the signature instance is used, and a ULID plus manifest digest is the last resort. The declared validation instant is recorded inside the package but is never used as its identifier.

functions.name: Record verification-method binding
functions.description: Attach a verification-method reference to a signature instance in its declared binding form, capturing the resolution inputs supplied, the resolution metadata returned and the version reference in effect. Does not perform resolution, does not create or update the external record, and does not judge the method's acceptability.
inputs: Resolution options supplied and resolution metadata returned by the external resolver
outputs: Verification-method binding record with pinned version reference
Declared purpose and mandatory relying-party feature fields extracted from the retrieved material
preconditions: The signature instance exists and is attachable by this mixin
The verification-method identifier is expressed in a namespace the adopting Dimension has declared in scope
effects: The signature instance gains a resolvable, version-pinned verification-method reference
Any purpose mismatch between the declared usage and the relied-on operation is flagged for the record, without an acceptance decision being made

functions.name: Record candidate paths and selection
functions.description: Record the candidate certification paths assembled toward a trust anchor, the retrieval source and observation time for each member certificate, and which candidate an external path builder selected on which recorded criteria. Does not build paths and does not execute path validation.
inputs: Candidate path descriptions supplied by an external path builder
Retrieval source and endpoint per member certificate
outputs: Candidate path records with ordered certificate references
Selected path reference with recorded selection criteria
Certification path certificate set artifact
preconditions: At least one candidate path has been supplied by an external builder
The binding form is one for which a certification path is meaningful
effects: Alternative paths remain visible rather than being silently discarded by the selection
The captured certificate set becomes replayable without re-contacting directories or authority information access endpoints

functions.name: Record path validation inputs and constraint outcomes
functions.description: Record the initial policy set, control flags and subtree inputs supplied for a determination, together with the per-certificate and per-path constraint outcomes reported back — basic constraints, name constraints, policy state and unrecognized critical extensions. The algorithm itself is executed by an external validator whose identity and version are recorded alongside.
inputs: Initial policy set, control flags, permitted and excluded subtrees
Constraint outcomes reported by the external validator
outputs: Constraint input record
Per-certificate and per-path constraint outcome record
preconditions: The reporting validator is identified so its outcomes are attributable
effects: The determination becomes reproducible because the exact inputs are retained beside the exact reported outcomes
Unrecognized critical extensions are recorded as facts rather than resolved into an acceptance verdict

functions.name: Pin trust-anchor and trust-store context
functions.description: Pin the trust anchor that terminated the selected path, its anchor-carried path controls, the trust store or trust list snapshot in force by sequence number, issue date-time and digest, and the service status observed for it. Does not admit, remove or supervise anchors and does not operate the trust list.
inputs: Trust anchor name and key identifier
Trust store or trust list location, sequence number, issue date-time and digest
Observed service status and its status starting date and time
outputs: Trust anchor context record
Trust-store snapshot pin
preconditions: The selected path terminates at an anchor present in a declared trust store or trust list
The snapshot digest was computed over the exact retrieved snapshot bytes
effects: A later reader can reproduce the anchor context by fetching the pinned issue and verifying the digest
A change of trust-store snapshot is detectable, because the pin differs even when the anchor name is unchanged

functions.name: Attach revocation status evidence
functions.description: Capture a signed status statement byte-preservingly, record its mechanism, reported value, reason, effective date, scope, this-update and next-update bounds, signer, delegation basis, nonce state, delivery channel and digest, and link it to the subject verification method. Does not request revocation, does not operate the responder or publisher, and does not interpret the value as an acceptance outcome.
inputs: Verification-method binding record or path certificate reference
Retrieved status evidence bytes and their retrieval endpoint
Status signer identity and reported delegation basis
outputs: Captured status evidence object artifact
Status determination record with freshness and scope fields
Status authorization and binding record
preconditions: The evidence claims a scope that covers the subject, or the out-of-scope condition is recorded explicitly
A digest over the exact retrieved bytes has been computed
effects: The status statement becomes independently re-verifiable from the retained bytes
A declared no-revocation-available or responder-no-check condition is recorded as a positive fact rather than as absent evidence

functions.name: Record an observed status transition
functions.description: Record that an authoritative source has reported a change in the subject's status — revocation, hold or release, supersession, or a compromise-driven reason change — with its published effective date and the separate time at which this model observed it. The transition itself is decided and published by the issuing authority; this function records the observation only.
inputs: Published effective date and reason code
outputs: Observed status transition record linking prior and new determinations
Updated reversibility and supersession fields
preconditions: Both the prior and the new determination are attributable to an authorized status signer for the subject
The published effective date is present or its absence is recorded
effects: Prior determinations are marked superseded rather than overwritten, preserving the historical view
Reversible states such as hold and release are distinguishable from permanent revocation in the retained history

functions.name: Declare the validation instant
functions.description: Declare which instant a trust-chain record is framed against — current time, best-signature time supported by a proof of existence, or a replayed historical instant — and record the clock-skew tolerance and time source used when comparing that instant to evidence windows. Does not issue proofs of existence and does not decide whether the framing yields an acceptable result.
inputs: Instant kind and instant value with seconds and an explicit offset
Proof-of-existence reference where the instant is in the past
Clock-skew tolerance and time source reference
outputs: Validation instant record
Comparison basis used against evidence this-update and next-update bounds
preconditions: A past instant is accompanied by a proof-of-existence reference, or the absence of one is recorded explicitly
The instant value carries seconds and an explicit offset
effects: Current-time framing, best-signature-time framing and historical replay are held as distinct records over the same evidence
Re-framing at a different instant produces a new record instead of mutating the existing one

functions.name: Assess record completeness and determinacy
functions.description: Classify this model's own record as determinate, evidence-incomplete or not assessed at the declared instant, by checking which required elements are present, stale, out of scope or unreachable, and carry any externally issued validation indication verbatim with its issuer. This is an assessment of evidence sufficiency in the record, not a trust decision, a policy evaluation or an enforcement action.
inputs: Trust-chain record with path, anchor and status evidence attached
Externally issued validation indication and sub-indication with issuer identity, where available
Declared failure-handling stance reference, where one has been declared elsewhere
outputs: Determinacy classification with per-element presence and staleness findings
Missing-element inventory with a reason for each entry
Carried indication fields attributed to their issuing validator
preconditions: A validation instant has been declared
Each element checked is either present with a verifiable digest or explicitly recorded as absent
effects: Missing or stale status evidence is recorded as evidence-incomplete and is never rewritten as a cryptographic failure or as a revocation
The declared failure-handling stance is carried as an attributed reference, leaving the accept-or-reject decision with the policy model that owns it

functions.name: Assemble a trust-chain replay package
functions.description: Assemble the selected path, anchor and trust-store pin, captured status evidence, declared instant, proof-of-existence references and determinacy record into a versioned, self-contained container that an external validator can re-evaluate later offline. Produces evidence for replay; it does not perform the replay and is not an audit record.
inputs: Package owner and requested package sequence number
outputs: Trust-chain evidence replay package artifact
Member manifest with per-member digests and pinned external references
preconditions: Every included member carries a digest that reproduces over its retained bytes
The determinacy classification for the declared instant is present, including where it reports evidence-incomplete
effects: A later determination at the same instant can proceed without contacting certificate authorities, responders, trust lists or resolvers
Export of the package is recorded with the requesting principal and declared purpose, with the audit entry itself held by the adopting Dimension's audit model

composition.purpose: WM-XCT-034 is registered as a child of WM-XCT-006 and inherits its broader cryptographic-trust framing. No relation rationale is published for this parent link and the registry review state is boundary-review-required, so the division of signature identity, algorithm and evidence concerns between parent and this mixin is provisional and must not be treated as settled.

composition.target: Signed subject model (any model whose records carry a signature or proof)
composition.purpose: Attach signature, trust-chain and status-evidence context to a subject record without altering, duplicating or constraining the subject's own semantics or lifecycle.

composition.target: Certificate authority and trust service operations model
composition.purpose: Carry references to issuers, responders, revocation records and their published effective dates. Issuance, the decision to revoke or suspend, responder operation and revocation publication remain owned there; this model records only observations and captured bytes.

composition.target: Trust list and trust anchor store governance model
composition.purpose: Pin the trust store or trust list snapshot by location, sequence number, issue date-time and digest, and record the service status observed. List issuance, supervision, qualification and status determination remain owned there.

composition.target: DID method registry and DID resolution model
composition.purpose: Reference verification methods by DID URL and carry the resolution options supplied, the resolution metadata returned and the version pinned. DID document lifecycle, deactivation and resolver operation remain owned there.

Reference the status list credential and index used for a credential-bound verification method and capture the value read. List construction, index assignment, publication cadence and herd-privacy sizing remain owned there.

Carry an attributed reference to the declared failure-handling stance for missing or stale status evidence. Evaluation of that stance, the accept-or-reject decision and any enforcement action remain owned there; this model records evidence completeness only.
Reference the proof of existence that fixes best-signature time or supports historical replay. Token issuance, timestamping authority trust and archival preservation remain owned there.

composition.target: Audit trail and event log model
composition.purpose: Locate audit entries for evidence captures and replay-package exports by reference. Audit record structure, tamper evidence, retention and query semantics remain owned there; referencing an audit record grants this model no audit-trail semantics.

composition.target: Cryptographic algorithm and suite registry model
composition.purpose: Reference signature, digest and key-agreement suite identifiers used by the signature and by the status evidence. Algorithm implementation, execution and deprecation scheduling remain owned there.

composition.target: RFC 5280 certification path validation and CRL profile
composition.purpose: Field-level alignment for path validation inputs, basic, name and policy constraints, key usage and extended key usage, and CRL evidence fields. Alignment only; no conformance is claimed absent a cited conformance test result.

composition.target: RFC 6960 Online Certificate Status Protocol and the RFC 9919 lightweight profile
composition.purpose: Field-level alignment for certificate identifier scope, status values, production and update times, responder authorization, nonce behaviour and caching. Alignment only; the profile version in use is recorded with each determination.

composition.target: ETSI EN 319 102-1 signature validation indications, as documented by the European Commission DSS reference implementation
composition.purpose: Carry the indication and sub-indication vocabulary verbatim, in particular the indeterminate cases that distinguish incomplete evidence from cryptographic failure. The ETSI normative text could not be retrieved directly, so this alignment is provisional and is not a conformance claim.

composition.target: W3C Bitstring Status List credential status model
composition.purpose: Field-level alignment for credential status entries, status purposes including the reversible suspension case, and status list validity and time-to-live fields. Alignment only.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension names an accountable owner for trust-chain and status evidence who is organizationally distinct from any certification authority, responder operator, trust-list scheme operator or credential issuer whose output the package captures.

The owner package enumerates which trust stores, trust lists and status mechanisms are in scope for its subjects, and pins each by identifier, version or sequence number, and digest; anchors outside that enumeration are recorded as out-of-scope rather than silently trusted.
The owner package names the external policy record that declares the failure-handling stance for missing or stale status evidence, and does not redefine that stance locally.
The owner package declares retention horizons for captured status evidence and replay packages, and names the records-management or archival service that executes disposition.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Local identifiers inside WM-XCT-034 use the sig-chain- prefix and are resolved under the adopting Dimension's namespace. External identifiers are carried verbatim in their originating namespace and are never re-minted locally: issuer name plus certificate serial number, CRL issuer plus CRL number, object identifier arcs for extensions and key purposes, DID URLs including any version parameters, status list credential URLs plus index, and trust list locations plus sequence numbers. Where the same anchor appears in two trust stores under different local handles, both handles are recorded and neither becomes canonical.
registry_links: Object identifier arcs for certificate extensions, key purposes and OCSP extensions as profiled by RFC 5280 and RFC 6960
W3C DID method registry entries referenced by verification-method DID URLs
EU List of Trusted Lists pointer entries and the national trusted list locations they carry
Root programme and CA/Browser Forum identifiers where publicly trusted TLS subjects are in scope

canonicalization_rules: Distinguished names, certificate serial numbers and key identifiers are stored in their canonical encoded form, with serial numbers hex-encoded without loss of leading zero octets, so that path and status records compare byte-exactly.

All recorded time values are normalized to RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset for comparison, while the original encoded form as retrieved is retained alongside so the source representation is never lost.
Captured evidence objects are stored byte-preserving; canonicalization is applied to the surrounding metadata record only and never to bytes covered by a signature.
Status vocabularies remain mechanism-scoped — CRL reason code, online status value, credential status purpose — and are never merged into a single cross-mechanism enumeration.
Trust-store pins are canonicalized as the tuple of location, sequence or version identifier, issue date-time and digest; a pin missing any element is incomplete rather than defaulted.
patch_rules: Captured evidence objects, their digests and their reported values are append-only; a correction adds a superseding capture and marks the prior record superseded, never editing it in place.
A change to the declared validation instant creates a new evaluation record rather than mutating the existing one, because the instant is what the determination is framed against.
Every patch records the observation time of the change and the identity of the recording system, held separately from the event time of the underlying fact.
Changing a trust-store snapshot pin, a selected path, or an anchor requires a new evaluation record, since the trust context differs even where the reported status is unchanged.
A carried external indication is never edited; a revised indication from the same validator is stored as a new attributed carry alongside the original.
compatibility_rules: Adding a new status mechanism, verification-method binding form or delivery channel code is a minor, backward-compatible change; removing or narrowing an existing status vocabulary is breaking.
Alignment mappings are versioned with the aligned standard's version, and an alignment change never silently reinterprets evidence already recorded under the earlier version.
Records created under a superseded protocol profile retain that profile's version reference so a historical replay reproduces the original interpretation rather than today's.
Consumers must tolerate an unknown determinacy reason code by treating the record as evidence-incomplete, never by promoting it to determinate.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier assigned by the issuing system: for a certificate, the issuer name plus certificate serial number; for a certificate revocation list, the CRL issuer plus CRL number; for a trusted list, the scheme operator plus TSL sequence number; for a signed online status response, the responder key identifier plus the certificate identifier and production time.

Governed global identifier or IRI where no master-system identifier exists: the DID URL of the verification method including its version parameter, the status list credential URL plus status list index, the trust list location, or the registered object identifier for an extension or key purpose.

UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension, used only as a last resort, and always recorded together with a digest over the exact retrieved bytes so the local handle can be re-bound if an authoritative identifier later becomes available.
A date, an issue time, a this-update or next-update value, a validity bound or a declared validation instant is never used as an identifier, even where it appears unique in practice.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All recorded time values use RFC 3339 with explicit seconds and an explicit UTC offset or Z. Event time — the time the underlying fact occurred or was published by its authoritative source, such as a revocation date, a CRL this-update or next-update, a response production time, or a trusted list issue date-time — is recorded separately from observation or ingestion time, meaning the time at which this model retrieved and captured the evidence. Both are held separately again from the declared validation instant the record is framed against, and from any proof-of-existence time. Where the source encodes time in a form without an offset, the normalized RFC 3339 value carries the resolved offset and the original encoded form is retained beside it.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serially issued evidence is named by its issuer plus its monotonic series number and never by its issue date: CRL issuer plus CRL number, trusted list scheme operator plus TSL sequence number, and replay package owner plus package sequence number. Gaps, out-of-order arrivals and re-issues within a series are recorded explicitly as observed, and members are never renumbered locally to close a gap. A delta series records its base series number so the pair is unambiguous.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every captured evidence object stores a digest over the exact retrieved bytes together with its digest algorithm identifier, and every replay package stores a manifest of member digests. A record whose digest does not reproduce is unusable for replay, and the mismatch is reported as an evidence-integrity fault attributable to storage or transport — never as a revocation, a cryptographic verification failure, or a trust outcome.

policies: External standards are recorded as alignments only. No conformance to RFC 5280, RFC 6960, RFC 9919, ETSI or W3C specifications is claimed without a cited conformance test result, and the ETSI alignment is explicitly marked provisional because its normative text was not directly retrievable.

Missing, stale, unreachable or out-of-scope status evidence is recorded as evidence-incomplete at the declared instant. It is never rewritten as a cryptographic failure and never presented as a revocation.

No single hard-fail, soft-fail or treat-as-unknown rule is embedded in this model. The applicable stance is carried as an attributed reference to the authority that declared it, and the accept-or-reject decision is made by the policy model that owns it.

A declared absence of revocation information — a no-revocation-available or responder-no-check declaration by the issuer — is recorded as a positive fact about the issuer's regime, and is distinguished from evidence that was expected but could not be obtained.

Status queries can expose relying-party behaviour, so the delivery channel is always recorded and privacy-preserving channels such as stapling and cached status lists are distinguishable from direct responder queries in every determination.

read: A read of a trust-chain record returns one consistent set: the selected path, the anchor and trust-store pin, every attached status evidence determination, the declared validation instant and the determinacy classification.

Historical reads are served by instant. A read framed at a past instant returns the evidence captured for that instant and its determinacy at that time, never the current live status silently substituted.

Reads never trigger live resolution of an external verification method, responder, trust list or status list. A read that would require live data returns evidence-incomplete with the missing element named, rather than blocking or fabricating a value.
Carried external indications are always returned with their issuing validator identity, version and policy reference, so they are never mistaken for a determination made by this model.
create: A trust-chain record is created only when a verification-method reference, a declared validation instant, and at least one status mechanism determination — including an explicit declared-unavailable or unreachable determination — are present.
Creation captures the exact retrieved bytes of each evidence object together with its digest and digest algorithm, its retrieval endpoint and its observation time.
Creation records the identity and version of every external component that supplied selection or outcome fields, so no unattributed assertion enters the record.
Where a candidate path was considered and rejected, it is created as a candidate record with its exclusion reason rather than being discarded.
update: Updates are additive. New evidence captures, new candidate paths and new evaluation records are appended, and superseded entries are marked superseded with the observation time of the supersession.
A recorded status value, reason code or effective date is never edited to reflect a later status; a later status is a new capture linked as an observed transition to the prior one.
Changing the trust-store snapshot pin, the selected path or the declared instant requires a new evaluation record, because the trust context of the determination has changed.
Digests are never recomputed over re-encoded bytes; if the retained bytes are lost, the record is marked evidence-destroyed rather than re-derived.
delete: Trust-chain and status-evidence records are retained for the retention horizon declared by the adopting Dimension, which must be at least as long as the longest replay obligation of the signatures they support. Where a responder publishes an archive-cutoff value, it is recorded as that responder's own lower bound on retained status information and never used to shorten the local horizon.

Deletion is by tombstone: the record identifier, its digests, its declared validation instant, its determinacy classification and the disposition reason are retained while the evidence payload is removed, so a later replay reports evidence-destroyed rather than evidence-never-existed.

Execution of deletion and disposition is owned by the adopting Dimension's retention and records-management policy, and for evidence held in external archives by the referenced archival and preservation model. This model owns only the tombstone it writes and the disposition reason it records; it neither schedules nor performs destruction.

Deletion, expiry or withdrawal of a referenced certificate, certificate revocation list, status response, status list or trust list at its source never propagates as a deletion here. The local capture and its digest remain, because a determination already framed at a past instant must stay replayable.
A replay package may be disposed of independently of its member records, but disposal records which members were included so the package cannot be silently reconstructed with a different membership.

roles.name: Trust-chain evidence owner
responsibilities: Accountable for the completeness and attribution of trust-chain records attached to the Dimension's signed subjects
Declares which trust stores, trust lists and status mechanisms are in scope and keeps their pins current
Approves the retention horizon and names the service that executes disposition

roles.name: Trust-anchor and trust-store curator
responsibilities: Maintains the enumeration of accepted anchors and their anchor-carried path controls
Pins each trust store or trust list issue by location, sequence number, issue date-time and digest, and records observed service status changes
Flags anchors that appear in a path but are absent from any declared store as out-of-scope

roles.name: Status-evidence collector
responsibilities: Captures status evidence byte-preservingly with digest, retrieval endpoint, delivery channel and observation time
Records nonce state, signer identity and reported delegation basis for every capture, including the explicit recursion-stop rule applied to the signer's own status
Records declared-unavailable regimes as positive facts, distinct from evidence that could not be obtained

roles.name: Validation-record steward and replay custodian
responsibilities: Declares validation instants, links proofs of existence and maintains the separation of event, observation and instant times
Assembles, versions and verifies replay packages, and approves their export
Maintains the determinacy classification and ensures evidence-incomplete outcomes are never restated as cryptographic failures

roles.name: Alignment and boundary reviewer
responsibilities: Reviews alignment mappings against the current versions of the aligned standards and records conflicts and supersessions
Confirms that no local finding or function has absorbed evaluation, execution, enforcement or audit-trail semantics belonging to a referenced model
Escalates the unresolved parent-model boundary with WM-XCT-006 and keeps the provisional status visible

access.default_rule: Trust-chain records are readable by principals already authorized to read the signed subject the mixin is attached to. The evidence adds no new subject content and grants no broader access than the subject itself carries.
exceptions: Records of direct status queries can reveal relying-party behaviour and transaction patterns; they are restricted to the status-evidence collector and the validation-record steward regardless of the subject's own access level.

Replay packages aggregate material that is otherwise separately controlled, including personal data appearing in end-entity subject names and alternative names; export requires the validation-record steward's approval and a declared purpose.
Trust-store snapshots and anchor sets for closed or private infrastructures may be operationally sensitive and can be restricted below the default rule at the curator's declaration.
Where a status response carries a nonce or correlation identifier that links a specific relying-party request, that field is restricted even when the surrounding determination is broadly readable.
audit_requirements: Every evidence capture records the retrieving principal or system, the endpoint used and the observation time.
Every export of a replay package records the requesting principal, the scope exported and the declared purpose.
Every tombstone records the disposition reason, the authorizing principal and the policy under which disposition was executed.

The audit records themselves are created, structured and retained by the adopting Dimension's audit model; this model stores only the references needed to locate them and asserts no audit-trail semantics of its own.

read_order: AGENTS.md — read Name, Type and the four URLs before touching any record, including when the store is MongoDB or the interface is MCP; the bootstrap contract is required regardless of projection.

Specification URL — read the scope statement, out-of-scope list and boundary notes to confirm the request belongs to this model rather than to a referenced certificate authority, trust-list, resolver, policy or audit model.
Storage type URL — read the projection details for the concrete store; JSON, YAML, Markdown, Git, MCP and MongoDB are projections and carry no semantics of their own.
Interface URL — read the available read and capture operations, in particular the rule that a read never triggers live external resolution and returns evidence-incomplete instead.
Processes URL — read the capture, instant-declaration, completeness-assessment, replay-assembly and tombstone procedures before creating or disposing of any record.

coverage.claim: This model states the context an agent needs to record, inspect and replay the trust-chain and revocation-status position of a digital signature or proof: how the verification method is referenced in each binding form, how it is reached from a pinned trust anchor under recorded constraints, what authorized status evidence says about it and how fresh that evidence is, which instant the record is framed against, and whether the evidence is complete enough to be determinate. It is grounded in RFC 5280 path validation and CRL profile, RFC 6960 with the RFC 9919 lightweight profile, RFC 4158 path building, RFC 5914 trust anchor format, RFC 9608 declared-unavailable revocation, RFC 7633 declared hard-fail, W3C DID and Bitstring Status List material, and European Commission trusted-list and validation-indication material. It does not claim conformance to any of them, does not claim to cover every trust model, and explicitly does not own certificate authority operation, trust-list operation, resolution, policy evaluation, cryptographic execution or audit-trail semantics.

checklist.notes: Identity priority runs from authoritative master-system identifiers (issuer plus serial, CRL issuer plus CRL number, scheme operator plus TSL sequence number, responder key identifier plus certificate identifier and production time) through governed IRIs (DID URLs, status list credential plus index, object identifiers) to Dimension-assigned ULIDs with digests. Dates, this-update values and validation instants are explicitly barred as identifiers.

Validity intervals, compromise, revocation, hold and release, and supersession are covered as observed transitions with published effective dates and separate observation times. The transitions themselves are decided and published by the issuing authority; this model records the observation and marks prior determinations superseded rather than overwriting them.

Verification method to signature, certificate to issuer along a path, anchor to trust store, status evidence to subject scope, status signer to its delegating authority, and proof of existence to instant are all modelled as explicit references with binding basis recorded.

Current time, best-signature time and historical replay are distinct instant kinds. Event time, observation or ingestion time, evidence this-update and next-update bounds, proof-of-existence time and the declared instant are held separately, all in RFC 3339 with seconds and explicit offsets, with clock-skew tolerance and time source recorded.

Retrieval source and endpoint per certificate, resolution options and returned metadata, path builder and validator identity and version, status signer and delegation basis, delivery channel and cache age, and per-object digests over exact retrieved bytes.

Controller and issuer references are recorded for verification methods; anchors carry their trust-store owner; status evidence carries its signer and delegating authority. Five roles assign local accountability, and every externally owned concern is routed to a composition link rather than modelled locally.

Constraint inputs and outcomes, evidence completeness, determinacy classification and verbatim attributed carriage of external indications are covered. Execution of path validation and cryptographic verification is explicitly external, and evidence-incomplete is kept structurally distinct from cryptographic failure.

Default rule inherits the signed subject's access. Four scopes are declared, with exceptions for query-behaviour records, replay-package export, closed-infrastructure anchor sets and nonce or correlation fields. Audit entries themselves are owned by the Dimension's audit model.

Retention horizon is declared by the adopting Dimension and must cover the longest replay obligation; a responder's archive-cutoff is a lower bound on the source side and never shortens the local horizon. Deletion is by tombstone preserving identifier, digests, instant, determinacy and disposition reason; execution is owned by the Dimension's records-management policy or the referenced archival model. Source-side deletion never propagates.

Mechanism-scoped status vocabularies are retained rather than normalized; profile versions are recorded with each determination; alignments to RFC, ETSI-derived and W3C vocabularies are versioned and marked as alignments only, with the ETSI alignment marked provisional.

CRL, delta CRL, online status protocol, credential status list and declared-unavailable regimes are all covered, with reason codes, reversibility, scope descriptors, responder authorization, nonce behaviour, stapling and freshness, and without selecting a universal hard-fail, soft-fail or unknown-handling policy.

Candidate and selected paths, retrieval provenance, loop control, initial policy and control-flag inputs, basic, name and policy constraint outcomes, unrecognized critical extensions, anchor-carried path controls, and trust-store snapshot pinning with observed service status.

This-update and next-update bounds, staleness measured against the declared instant, cache age, clock-skew tolerance and time source are all recorded as measurable quantities rather than as a binary fresh or stale flag.

Delivery channel distinguishes privacy-preserving stapling and cached lists from direct queries; query-behaviour records and nonce or correlation fields carry access exceptions. Herd-privacy sizing of status lists is referenced but owned by the publication model.

Scheme territory appears in trust-list pins, but there is no worked treatment of jurisdictional recognition, cross-border trust-list bridging or conflicting national qualification regimes. Recorded as a gap rather than presented as covered.

Suite identifiers are referenced to an external algorithm registry, but hybrid and post-quantum signature migration raises trust-chain questions — mixed-suite paths, dual signatures on status evidence, re-anchoring of long-lived proofs — that no retrieved primary source in this evidence base resolves. Recorded as a gap.

known_omissions: The rationale for the registered parent relation to WM-XCT-006 is not published and the registry review state is boundary-review-required, so the division of signature identity, algorithm and evidence concerns between parent and this mixin is provisional.
Certificate Transparency log inclusion and consistency proofs are not modelled as a trust-chain or status mechanism.
Attribute certificates and authorization-only chains are not distinguished from public-key certificate chains.
Delta CRL reconstruction state and CRL scope arithmetic are referenced through the scope descriptor but are not decomposed into their own finding.
Non-X.509 chain models such as web-of-trust and simple public key infrastructure are outside the retrieved evidence base.
Device and hardware attestation chains are reached only through the generic verification-method binding, without their own manufacturer-anchor semantics.
Cross-certification and bridge trust topologies are acknowledged as producing multiple candidate paths but their policy-mapping arithmetic is not modelled in field-level detail.
Short-lived certificate regimes that intentionally dispense with revocation are covered only through the declared-unavailable path, not as a distinct issuance strategy.
conflicts: RFC 5019 was obsoleted by RFC 9919, which changes hash-algorithm guidance and restates nonce handling; lightweight-profile behaviour must therefore be recorded together with the profile version rather than assumed, and older records must retain the profile they were made under.

RFC 6960 treats unknown as a first-class status distinct from good and revoked, while RFC 9608 directs relying parties to skip revocation checking entirely when a no-revocation-available declaration is present. The model records both without collapsing declared-unavailable into unknown.

CRL certificateHold expresses a reversible suspension with no direct equivalent in the online status protocol's three values, while Bitstring Status List models suspension as a separate reversible status purpose. Mechanism-specific vocabularies are retained rather than normalized into one enumeration.

RFC 7633 makes hard-fail well-founded only where the certificate itself declares the required feature, whereas CA/Browser Forum operational practice for publicly trusted TLS reflects a different stance. Neither is treated as the model's default.

ETSI EN 319 102-1, TS 119 612 and TS 119 615 normative texts could not be retrieved directly — etsi.org returned HTTP 403 for its published deliverables — so the indication and sub-indication vocabulary and trusted-list field semantics are grounded in European Commission first-party documentation and the live EU List of Trusted Lists. That alignment is provisional and is flagged as such rather than presented as verified.

DID Resolution v1.0 is a Candidate Recommendation Draft and DIDs v1.1 is a Candidate Recommendation; resolution metadata and version-parameter details may still change, so those fields are recorded as alignment targets at a stated draft date rather than as stable structure.

The live EU List of Trusted Lists retrieved for this model exposed sequence and version identifiers but the list issue date-time and next-update elements were not observable in the retrieved excerpt, so the trust-store pin treats issue date-time as required by the pin contract while noting that its presence was not directly confirmed in that observation.
regional_assumptions: Trust-list semantics are grounded in the EU List of Trusted Lists and its ETSI profile. Other jurisdictions operate different trust-list, root-programme or bridge models, and the snapshot pin fields must be re-bound to whatever series identifier and issue metadata those schemes publish.

CA/Browser Forum requirements apply to publicly trusted TLS server certificates and are not normative for enterprise, government, device or closed-community infrastructures; treating their operational stance as a default would be a category error.

Retention horizons for revocation evidence and replay packages are jurisdiction- and sector-specific. The model records the horizon reference and leaves its determination to the adopting Dimension's records-management policy.

Explicit UTC offsets are required rather than assumed because validation instants, evidence windows and proofs of existence are routinely compared across jurisdictions and across systems with different local clocks.
Privacy expectations around status queries differ materially by jurisdiction; the model records the delivery channel so that a Dimension can apply its own local rule rather than inheriting one.
adversarial_checks: Checked that no finding or function claims ownership of path-validation execution. The constraint finding records inputs supplied and outcomes reported with the reporting validator's identity and version; no function performs the RFC 5280 algorithm, and the cryptographic verification outcome is carried as a separate attributed field.

Checked that OCSP responder operation and certificate authority revocation execution are not modelled locally. Delegated signing and the delegated signing purpose appear only as a recorded authorization basis for evidence already produced elsewhere, never as a capability this model exercises.

Rejected an attractive standalone revocation-lifecycle layer. The transition from valid to revoked, held or superseded is decided and published by the issuing authority, so only observed transitions with published effective dates and separate observation times are carried, and prior determinations are superseded rather than rewritten.

Tested the counterexample of a certificate carrying a no-revocation-available declaration, where absent status evidence is normatively correct rather than a gap. The determinacy classification therefore distinguishes declared-unavailable from expected-but-missing, and a policy that treated the two identically would misread the record.

Tested the counterexample of an expired or later-revoked certificate whose signature remains sound at best-signature time given a proof of existence. Current-time framing, best-signature-time framing and historical replay are held as separate records over the same evidence rather than collapsed into a single verdict field.

Rejected asserting any universal hard-fail, soft-fail or treat-as-unknown rule. RFC 7633 makes hard-fail well-founded only where declared in the certificate, while publicly trusted TLS practice reflects a different stance, so the stance is carried as an attributed external reference and the decision stays with the policy model.

Checked that no bundle or artifact absorbs audit-trail semantics. The replay package is an evidence container assembled from this model's own captures; audit entries for captures and exports are located by reference and are structured and retained by the Dimension's audit model.

Checked the exclusive representation rule across all nine findings: the three findings declaring artifacts hold retrieved bytes this model genuinely custodies, and the six inline findings are reference, scalar or outcome data whose underlying bytes are either externally owned or already retained by an artifact in the same layer.

Checked that the trust-store pin does not become a local copy of a trust list. The pin is location, sequence number, issue date-time, digest and observed status; a consumer needing the bytes fetches the pinned issue from its operator and verifies the digest, which keeps list issuance and status determination with the scheme operator.
